text: All athletic horses are fast and strong-willed.

origin.adaptation: None: exact isolated source sentence, punctuation and both predicate conjuncts retained.

notes: One universally bound horse, head-before-modifier antecedent. Athletic is intersective property under fixed-context extensional reading; fast and strong-willed both consequent properties. Hyphenated adjective retained as one lexical predicate, no omitted conjunction. No existential import.

semantics_contract.lexical_policy: horse singular lemma; strong-willed atomic lexical adjective; fixed-context property reading

text: Every bird either knows the troposphere or reveres Joziah (or both).

origin.adaptation: None: exact isolated source sentence including either and explicit or both; same source record as prior simplified/query universal control, distinct full theory sentence.

notes: Inclusive scope disjunction within one universal. Both transitive predicates retain subject-first arguments. Know takes an object (acquaintance/knowledge-of relation), not a proposition: no factive content projection. The troposphere uses an explicit definite-description constant troposphere; existence/uniqueness not separately represented in this project contract. No whole-NP existential simplification or disjunct deletion.

semantics_contract.definite_policy: the troposphere is one fixed contextually identified referent, canonical constant troposphere; no independently asserted existence/uniqueness claims
semantics_contract.disjunction_policy: or both is inclusive; either metadata records surface marker only
semantics_contract.lexical_policy: extensional transitive know-of relation; not sentential know-that
